name: Neuromodulation: gain and time constants conditioned on scene state (octopamine)
essence: Add a small modulator that reads a causal scene-state vector (mean luminance, contrast, glare fraction, ego-motion speed of the camera) and outputs global per-cell-type multipliers for FlyVis: a gain and a time-constant factor for each of the 65 types (about 130 numbers), applied on top of the fixed connectome and the trained parameters. Biological analogue: during flight octopaminergic neurons raise the gain of motion-sensitive neurons and speed up the inputs of T4/T5 (Mi1, Tm3, Mi4, Mi9), shifting temporal tuning towards higher frequencies. Engineering analogues are FiLM-style conditioning and neuromodulated networks, image-adaptive parameter prediction (IA-YOLO) and darkness prompts for a frozen tracker (DCPT). A zero-training variant sets the multipliers by hand from the biology (faster time constants at high ego-speed, higher gain in the dark).
sources: Maimon, Straw & Dickinson, Active flight increases the gain of visual motion processing in Drosophila, Nat Neurosci 2010; Suver et al., Octopamine Neurons Mediate Flight-Induced Modulation of Visual Processing in Drosophila, Curr Biol 2012, https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0960982212012559; Arenz et al., The Temporal Tuning of the Drosophila Motion Detectors Is Determined by the Dynamics of Their Input Elements, Curr Biol 2017, https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0960982217300866; Strother et al., Behavioral state modulates the ON visual motion pathway of Drosophila, PNAS 2018, https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.1703090115; Chiappe et al., Walking modulates speed sensitivity in Drosophila motion vision, Curr Biol 2010; Octopaminergic modulation of temporal frequency tuning of a fly visual motion-sensitive neuron depends on adaptation level, 2015, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26074790/; Octopaminergic modulation of the visual flight speed regulator of Drosophila, J Exp Biol 2014, https://journals.biologists.com/jeb/article/217/10/1737/14000; Vecoven, Ernst, Wehenkel, Drion, Introducing neuromodulation in deep neural networks to learn adaptive behaviours, PLoS ONE 2020, https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0227922; Perez et al., FiLM: Visual Reasoning with a General Conditioning Layer, AAAI 2018; Liu et al., Image-Adaptive YOLO for Object Detection in Adverse Weather Conditions, AAAI 2022, https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.08088; Zhu et al., DCPT: Darkness Clue-Prompted Tracking in Nighttime UAVs, ICRA 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.10491; Lappalainen et al., Nature 2024 (FlyVis), https://github.com/TuragaLab/flyvis.
relevance: Addresses the regime mismatch of a frozen FlyVis trained on Sintel: H9 (night input; complements the retina, which handles luminance but not temporal regime), the speed/scale regime limit (Neuroinformatics 2026: frozen FlyVis direction decoding collapses at the upper aperture scale), and H11 (functions where the fly is 'native', e.g. ego-motion with a moving dashcam). BDD100K has large variation of camera speed and illumination within and between videos; per-track foveal crops change apparent speed with object distance. Indirect relevance for IDSw through signatures that are more stable across scene regimes.
novelty_overlap: [uncertain] Neuromodulation / conditioning of network parameters by context is well established in ML (FiLM 2018, Vecoven et al. 2020, hypernetworks) and in low-light CV (IA-YOLO predicts filter parameters from the image; DCPT injects darkness prompts into a frozen tracker). State-dependent gain and temporal tuning of fly motion vision are established biology (Maimon 2010, Suver 2012, Arenz 2017, Strother 2018). No work was found that applies state-conditioned per-type multipliers to FlyVis or to a connectome-constrained model inside a tracker; the idea is listed in the project's own note (Исследование_модернизация_мухи.md, section 6). cannot_claim: the neuromodulation concept, the conditioning mechanism, and physiological fidelity (octopamine receptors act on specific types such as Mi4 per Strother 2018, whereas a global multiplier on all 65 types is an engineering abstraction).
author_results: [uncertain] Suver 2012: octopamine neurons are necessary and sufficient for the flight-induced boost of VS-cell responses; the boost is largest at temporal frequencies of about 2-8 Hz and a gain increase from about 2.2 to 5.5 (about 150%) is reported (numbers from search summaries, not re-verified in the full text). Maimon 2010: flight increases the gain of visual motion responses in VS cells. Arenz 2017: the octopamine agonist chlordimeform shifts T4/T5 temporal tuning to higher frequencies, fully explained by faster input elements (calcium imaging). Strother 2018: behavioural state changes baseline and temporal tuning of T4 and its inputs Mi1, Tm3, Mi4, Mi9, most strongly in Mi4, which receives octopaminergic input. Vecoven 2020: neuromodulated networks adapt better across task distributions in meta-RL benchmarks (no vision numbers). IA-YOLO 2022: 165K-parameter predictor of filter parameters, ExDark mAP 36.42 to 40.37, RTTS 28.82 to 37.08. DCPT 2024: prompts for a frozen daytime UAV tracker reach state of the art on dark benchmarks (numbers not verified). Biology uses tethered flies with controlled stimuli; CV numbers are single images (IA-YOLO) or 30 fps UAV video with moving camera (DCPT); none is dashcam MOT.
measured_level: Biology: single-neuron electrophysiology and calcium imaging; ML: task reward; CV: detection mAP (IA-YOLO) and single-object success/precision (DCPT). No MOT HOTA/IDF1 evidence. In the project the first test would be pair-level AP (reliability head on dark/bright dev+test, re-ID head), then HOTA only if pair-level CI > 0.
matched_control: None of the literature has a same-information control. Required here: (1) give the readout head the same scene-state vector directly (tests whether modulating inside the fly beats simply informing the head); (2) state-independent learned multipliers with the same parameter count (tests conditioning vs extra capacity); (3) modulator driven by a scene state shuffled across videos; (4) the same modulator on the degree- and sign-preserving shuffled connectome (as in fly_connectome_null_v1); (5) frozen fly with retina-lamina as the baseline. The project's existing matched controls (fly_matched_controls_v1, fly_connectome_null_v1) define the standard.
conditions_breakdown: Biology: flight vs quiescence (or walking), temporal frequency. IA-YOLO: fog vs low light. Project: dark vs bright split exists; an ego-speed split (from the camera-motion estimate already computed for the tracker) and a glare split would be new and are the natural strata for this mechanism.
cost_here: [uncertain] Zero-training variant: hand-set multipliers for time constants and gains by luminance/ego-speed bins, recomputation of fovea outputs on val7 then dark+bright dev/test (about 1 GPU hour per setting, same class as the retina runs), evaluation on CPU with the existing heads. Trained variant: needs the same differentiable FlyVis training infrastructure as C4/M2 (not yet in the project) and re-rendered foveal hex-input sequences; about 130 parameters plus a tiny MLP, so training cost is at most that of M2 (3-6 GPU hours) per configuration, plus the controls. Scene-state features are cheap: mean luminance per frame is already used for the dark/bright split; ego-motion can come from existing DIS/ECC estimates.
expected_effect: [uncertain] Small at pair level (at most a few thousandths of AP), because the fly adds little over DIS and the lamina already handles luminance; the most plausible gain is in speed-dependent regimes (fast ego-motion, near objects) and in any future ego-motion or looming readout (C6/C7) rather than in the current reliability head. No HOTA effect is expected unless the pair-level CI is clearly positive.
risks: (1) Extra parameters confound the comparison; controls (2)-(3) in matched_control are mandatory. (2) The modulator can learn video identity if the state vector is too rich; keep it low-dimensional and causal (only past frames). (3) Scaling time constants towards the integration step (2 steps per 30 Hz frame) can destabilise the Euler dynamics; clamp multipliers. (4) Rapid state changes (tunnels, oncoming headlights) require smoothing that itself adds lag. (5) Claims of octopamine fidelity are not supportable with a global multiplier. (6) Rule compliance: detector frozen (untouched), one condition changed per comparison, paired per-video bootstrap, tuning on train/val only; GPU runs over 1 h need user approval.
attribution: Borrowed: biological motivation (Maimon et al. 2010; Suver et al. 2012; Arenz et al. 2017; Strother et al. 2018); conditioning mechanism (FiLM, Perez et al. 2018; neuromodulated networks, Vecoven et al. 2020; image-adaptive parameter prediction, Liu et al. 2022; darkness prompts, Zhu et al. 2024); FlyVis model (Lappalainen et al. 2024). Ours: state-conditioned per-type gain and time-constant multipliers on a per-track foveal FlyVis eye for dashcam MOT, the choice of scene-state variables, the control set and the evaluation.
